name: Carolingian Renaissance under Alcuin
summary: Alcuin of York, recruited by Charlemagne to direct the palace school at Aachen, oversees a systematic recovery of classical Latin learning. Standardised Caroline minuscule script, the trivium-quadrivium curriculum, and copying programmes preserve most surviving Latin classical texts.

_quarry.structural_significance: Without the Carolingian copying programme roughly half the Latin classical corpus would not have survived. Caroline minuscule becomes the foundation of modern lower-case Western script; every Roman font derives from it.
